languageModelTools.name: bonsai_generate_context
languageModelTools.userDescription: Generate self-contained Bonsai context files for the current workspace.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Generate or update self-contained Bonsai repository context files in the active VS Code workspace. Use this when bonsai.xml or bonsai.json does not exist, or when the existing context is stale, before answering broad repository questions. Call this tool instead of a VS Code command. The request field is required. Bonsai ranks likely files from request terms, declared symbols, imports, callers, and nearby tests; it works even before the agent knows exact files. When the agent has inspected likely files, it may pass filePriorities with exact workspace-relative paths: level 1 for primary code, level 2 for supporting structure, and level 3 for compact background context. Treat a plan as a hint, not proof: Bonsai keeps request-derived candidates and related dependencies protected too. Level 1 drops comments by default; set includeComments true only when comments are needed. Bonsai validates any planned paths before writing. If this tool is unavailable because the user has not enabled it, tell the user to open VS Code Agent mode, select Select Tools, and enable Generate Bonsai Context, or explicitly reference #bonsai_generate_context in chat. It scans supported source files, always ignores common dependency and build directories such as node_modules and target, respects .gitignore and .cursorignore, compresses content to the configured token budget, and writes bonsai.xml or bonsai.json plus numbered chunks under 10 MB each. It returns the generated file paths and the first context file contents. Do not use it for narrow questions that do not need broad repository context.

workspacePath.description: Optional absolute path of an open workspace folder. Omit it to use the active workspace.

request.description: Short summary of the user's repository question or task. Matching modules receive more detail.

filePriorities.description: Optional agent-selected workspace-relative files and requested detail levels. Bonsai also derives candidates from the request.

level.description: 1 = nearly full source, 2 = signatures and structure, 3 = compact map.

reason.description: Why this file matters for the user's request.

includeComments.description: Keep comments for this file at level 1. Defaults to false for agent-selected primary files.

bonsai.maxTokens.description: Token budget for generated Copilot context. Project .bonsai.toml can set max_tokens.

bonsai.level.description: Compression: 1 full source first, 2 signatures and shapes, 3 names and tree map. Start with 2.

bonsai.outputFile.description: File path where generated context is written.

bonsai.outputFormat.description: Generated context format. The extension supports XML and JSON.

bonsai.include.description: Optional glob patterns to include, such as src/**.

bonsai.exclude.description: Optional glob patterns to exclude, such as **/generated/**.

scripts.test: npm run compile && node dist/bonsai.smoke.test.js && node dist/internalGenerator.smoke.test.js
